Hold the existing US and Australian pays. Cut half the remaining Canada pay after March CORRA cheapened from 3.125 to 2.905, while cash at 2.28 still leaves some residual tightening.

trend-follower.thesis: The book remains short 75 million March 2027 SOFR from 4.62 versus a live 4.515 print, with cash at 3.87, the US ten-year at 5.21, and Brent at 105.69. Williams seeing no 2027 hike while still calling for one more 2026 hike is pullback risk, not a trend break, because December 2026 still sits at 4.25. Covering 4.515 would fade a higher-for-longer path that oil and the long end still support.

cross_market_rv.rationale: Cash NZ minus US 10-year at minus 23 basis points is the first percentile of one-year history and the 0.3rd percentile of five-year history, with a 13 January 2025 analog that reversed after the same 30 basis-point one-month cheapening.

curve.rationale: New Zealand 2s10s at 118 basis points is a steep domestic curve, not the US-relative cheapness that needs to converge.

five_year.rationale: Cash NZ minus US 5-year is minus 58 basis points and even more extreme on percentile, but the 5 June 2026 analog kept cheapening, and 5-year sits closer to policy than the 10-year cash screen.

rates_tenor_scan.selection_rationale: After scanning STIR, 2-year, 5-year, outright 10-year, and curve, the cleanest rates expression is the cash NZ minus US 10-year peer spread.

stir_policy_path.rationale: Cash-versus-strip in SOFR, CORRA, and AONIA is already the crowded desk book. New Zealand has no OCR strip in the tradable paper-rate universe, so a short-end pack cannot express this peer dislocation.

ten_year.rationale: Outright New Zealand 10-year is the 93rd percentile of its own history and US 10-year is the 96th. Neither cash 10-year is cheap in isolation; the dislocation is the peer spread.

two_year.rationale: Cash NZ minus US 2-year is already minus 99 basis points at the 2nd percentile. A 2-year cross-market spread is not cheap because the kiwi is cheap; after that cash screen the 2-year pack is not the residual.

expression_memo.rationale: The mispricing is the cash 10-year peer spread, not kiwi cheapness. Rates is cleaner than spot because NZ minus US 10-year is independently extreme after screening cash 2-year, and New Zealand is now eligible.

spot_candidate.rationale: Long kiwi versus the dollar at 0.5613, the 2.8th percentile, is the FX residual after the cash 2-year screen. It imports oil and dollar beta the 10-year cash spread does not need.

value-guy.thesis: New Zealand's 10-year cash yield is 4.98 percent against the US 10-year at 5.21 percent, so NZ minus US 10-year sits at minus 23 basis points, the first percentile of one-year history and the 0.3rd percentile of five-year history, after a 30 basis-point one-month cheapening in which the US 10-year rose 25 basis points and New Zealand's 10-year fell only 3. That is a cash peer-duration dislocation, not a 2-year pack because the kiwi is cheap: cash NZ minus US 2-year is already minus 99 basis points, and kiwi at 0.5613 is a separate spot residual. Convergence is pay New Zealand 10-year versus receive US 10-year so the spread rises toward its historical New Zealand premium; the 13 January 2025…

vol-convexity.invalidation: This HOLD is wrong if a later freeze shows a markable options structure with premium, implied vol, and strikes whose convex payoff rates and spot cannot express, and last-resort use is then required.
vol-convexity.thesis: This book is flat. The VIX is 15.21 and the S&P is near 7805, and rates and spot already express the oil and policy tape. A volatility clip is not a last-resort case here because this freeze does not name a markable convex payoff that linear rates or spot fail to express. Stay at the zero cash benchmark rather than paying funding on an unmarkable options clip.
